newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bills break resistance level after sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bills break resistance level after sale.

text.p: Yields of Russian long-term GKO discount Treasury bills broke through resistance at 19 percent on Thursday after Wednesday's auctions yields were higher than the average market levels, dealers said.
*Average yield on taxable T-bills rose to 19.38 pct from 18.81 pct on Tuesday
*Average yield on taxable floating-rate OFZ bonds was 32.15 pct after 29.05 pct
*Turnover rose to 4.56 bln rbls from 4.10 trln rbls

"Most likely today's GKO rise was a reaction to the auctions," Rossiisky Kredit dealer Konstantin Svyatny said.

"Yesterday the Finance Ministry let us feel that we could raise the yield and in conditions of an obvious fall in foreign interest there is no one to support the market. Our small and meduim-sized banks have run off to the share market and the big ones do not have free money."
On Wednesday the highest accepted yield on an issue of 364-day T-billa was 19.27 percent, the highest since mid-July, and on a 182-day T-bill was 19.33 percent.
"Most operators expected a slight fall in prices and one big bank was probably withdrawing funds, which made today's fall worse," said Bank Imperial dealer Sergei Gubanov.
Dealers said the trend in the next few days would depend on how active the central bank would be operating on the market.
On the foreign exchange market, dealers said high overnight credit rates persisted as a big bank bought roubles on the market for a second day in a row.

"Overnight has been growing for the whole day, first of all on purchases of biggest banks," a dealer said. "Only an obvious lack of liquidity can make a bank to borrow money at a rate higher than a central bank refinancing rate."

The central bank's refinancing rate is currently 24 percent. The central bank does not actually lend money at the refinancing rate, which usually acts as a ceiling for market rates, although overnight credits can go over it.
